html:
SMTO-CFG-0092 — SMTO couldn't tell whether you allowed the Skill

GUID: c6c3d264-11f0-59c6-96e6-0163e98e7d35
Slug: capability-activation-grant-ambiguous
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: capability_activation

What happened

  • Your reply to the Skill permission question wasn't a clear yes or no, so no permission was given. The Skill was not turned on.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the question is still showing under the task, select Allow for this conversation (or Allow for this task) or Don't allow instead of typing. The buttons send a clear decision, and SMTO never guesses permission from loosely worded text.
  2. If you prefer typing, reply with just one word such as yes, allow, no or deny, and nothing else. SMTO only recognizes a few exact replies as a decision; anything longer counts as unclear.
  3. If the question is gone and you did want the Skill, turn it on in Capabilities in the message box controls, then send a new message asking SMTO to use it. An unclear answer counts as a no for this request, so SMTO won't ask again until there is a new request.

What success looks like

  • The question disappears, and the task either uses the Skill or carries on without it, matching your answer.

If it still fails

  • If the buttons don't respond or this message keeps returning, select Copy error details in this panel and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste long text into the permission question; it never counts as approval.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The capability grant decision was not an explicit allow or deny: a structured capability_decision outside allow/deny was rejected, or reply text matched no recognized approval or denial phrase and was recorded as ambiguous; no capability permission was granted.

What this means

  • A supplied structured capability decision is outside allow/deny, or deterministic text interpretation yields no recognized approval/denial. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • A supplied structured capability decision is outside allow/deny, or deterministic text interpretation yields no recognized approval/denial.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the current exact question and supported decision controls; ambiguous text must not be treated as consent.

How to fix it

  • Submit capability_decision as exactly allow or deny with the matching capability_grant_request_id, or reply text of yes, allow, no or deny. An ambiguous text reply is recorded as grant state ambiguous and later classified as grant_declined for the same task source, so a new request is needed to prompt again.
  • Use the current capability question's explicit allow or deny control.

Retry and execution caution

  • The reported capability or interaction condition changes.

How to verify the fix

  • An explicit matching allow/deny decision is accepted, with no authority inferred from ambiguity.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass frozen authority, operation permissions or credential requirements.

Technical notes

  • The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
